routes.description: Establish that claims of origin-of-life progress substantially exceed what current chemical evidence supports by distinguishing demonstrated precursor phenomena from an integrated, self-replicating cellular system and by testing whether public descriptions preserve those limitations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the remaining gaps in integration, cellular organization, replication, and experimental relevance are central to explaining life's emergence, while claims of proximity or understanding communicate more confidence than the evidence warrants.

motionBridge.description: Show that representations of current progress imply substantially greater explanatory proximity than demonstrated results justify.

centralBridges.description: Establish that evidence for simple molecules or isolated chemical behaviors does not yet bridge the transition to autonomous cellular life.
Require credible coordination of synthesis, purification, metabolism, compartmentalization, information, and continued replication under compatible conditions.
Connect technical limitations to claims made to nonspecialists, students, or scientists about how much of life's emergence is understood.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate criticism of present evidence from any assertion that a future naturalistic explanation is impossible or that ignorance establishes design.
Require explicit criteria distinguishing life from isolated lifelike chemical activity before treating experiments as proximity to life.

routes.description: Establish that a testable pathway is emerging by identifying reproducible transitions from simple chemistry to templating, information, autocatalytic cooperation, replication, and increasing complexity, without requiring reconstruction of Earth's unique molecular history or a completed laboratory creation of life.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if current theory and experiments provide falsifiable, cumulative footholds toward general laws of life's emergence and the qualified claim of an emerging pathway does not imply that the full mechanism is already known.

motionBridge.description: Show that appropriately qualified claims of a testable emerging pathway track substantive evidence and therefore are not substantially overstated.

centralBridges.description: Demonstrate experimentally accessible processes by which simple chemistry generates templates, coupled catalytic behavior, information, or other increasing complexity.
Provide testable steps from nonliving chemistry toward imperfect replication, heredity, evolution, primitive cells, or essential cellular machinery.
Frame the observed steps within an objective and falsifiable theory of chemical complexity rather than an unsupported historical narrative.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use geological, meteoritic, and cosmological evidence to constrain the simple initial chemistry and timing without claiming an exact molecular sequence.
Preserve distinctions among indications, testable pathways, completed explanations, and actual creation or detection of life.

sections.title: Claims of progress and the standard for explanation
sections.rationale: The motion turns first on what researchers claim to understand and whether an emerging, falsifiable pathway is being represented as a completed account of life's origin.

sections.title: From simple chemistry to information-bearing complexity
sections.rationale: Evidence about early simple materials, molecular templating, autocatalytic sets, and objective complexity bears directly on whether experiments establish a meaningful natural progression rather than isolated chemistry.

sections.title: Transition to integrated cellular organization
sections.rationale: The central explanatory distance concerns whether separate chemical achievements can be joined into an autonomous system with boundaries, material organization, metabolism, resource flows, and cellular function.

sections.title: Replication, heredity, and criteria for life
sections.rationale: Competing accounts emphasize replication as a threshold while disputing whether fidelity, repeated copying, functional information, evolution, and explicit criteria are necessary before a system counts as approaching life.

sections.title: Experimental method, falsifiability, and warranted inference
sections.rationale: The weight of current progress depends on experimental assumptions, researcher-supplied conditions, prebiotic relevance, theory–experiment iteration, and the permissible inference from controlled results to a general origin pathway.
